sonnet.q1: It rejects malformed events individually, lists them in the response, and still accepts the rest of the batch. It returns 202 only after the log confirms the write is replicated.
sonnet.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, backing off exponentially from 1 s up to 5 minutes.
sonnet.q3: The first copy received (earliest received_at, ties broken by log order). Later copies are dropped from events_clean.
sonnet.q4: The UTC day of received_at, so Tuesday's partition and Tuesday's replay. The client timestamp is not used.
sonnet.q5: In the KV store (key-value store with per-key TTL). Each event_id is recorded as a key, claimed set-only-if-absent. Keys expire after 8 days (TTL).
sonnet.q7: NOT STATED. The document only covers a crash between claiming and loading (event missing until replay). It says the processor records its position after the load, but not how the crash after load and before recording is handled.
sonnet.q8: It reads the archive files for the replayed day and the 7 days before it (never the log). Results are written to a staging table, then atomically swapped into the day's partition of events_clean.
sonnet.q9: It reads the archive for day D and the 7 prior days, deduplicates by event_id keeping the earliest received_at (ties by log order), and keeps an event only if its first copy falls on day D. Events first received on an earlier day are dropped.
sonnet.q10: Nothing is swapped, so the old partition stays unchanged. The operator fixes the cause and reruns.
sonnet.q11: Closed days only (ended at least 2 hours ago, closing at 02:00 UTC the next day) whose archive files still exist (within 90 days). One replay runs at a time.
sonnet.q12: Not decided. Product has not chosen whether to drop bots or keep them with a flag. Detection would run in the enrichment step of both live path and replay.
